name: Slack
summary: Easy for your own workspace and for unlisted installs in other workspaces. Reading message history at scale or using Slack's hosted MCP server outside your own workspace pushes you into a Slack Marketplace review that needs 10 active workspaces and can take weeks.

verdicts.why: An app that stays in your own workspace needs no review: create it, add scopes, install it.
Installing in other workspaces means turning on public (unlisted) distribution and building a full OAuth flow; Slack documents a review only for the Marketplace, not for unlisted apps.

verdicts.waiting: Up to 10 business days, then up to 10 weeks
verdicts.why: Unlisted apps get 1 request per minute on message history and cannot use Slack's MCP server, so a real launch needs Slack Marketplace approval, which needs 10 active workspaces and a demo video first.

skip.note: Composio runs its own Slack app, so you can skip registering one. Slack's hosted MCP server does not support dynamic client registration, so MCP clients need a registered app's client ID and secret.
whyOwnApp: Composio's managed app is still going through Marketplace review, so strict workspaces may need an admin to approve it.
Composio calls your own app the recommended and safest option for a workspace.
Using Slack's MCP server needs your own internal or Marketplace app; there is no dynamic registration.

requirements.label: A Slack workspace you can install apps into
requirements.detail: You create the app at api.slack.com/apps and pick a workspace to develop it in.

requirements.label: An HTTPS redirect URL
requirements.detail: The redirect URL in your app settings and the redirect_uri you send must both use HTTPS.

requirements.label: SSL on every app URL
requirements.detail: Public distribution needs SSL on your OAuth redirect, interactivity, options load and Events API URLs.

requirements.label: Privacy policy and public landing page
requirements.detail: Marketplace apps need a privacy policy that covers collection, use, retention and deletion, linked from a public landing page built for the Slack app.

requirements.label: A public support contact
requirements.detail: An email or contact form that needs no extra account, with replies expected within 2 business days.

requirements.label: 10 or more active workspaces
requirements.detail: The app must already be installed on 10+ workspaces used in the past 28 days before you can submit to the Marketplace.

requirements.label: Review demo video
requirements.detail: Show install, OAuth, setup, end-to-end use and uninstall, with no code editors, terminals or marketing intros.

requirements.label: A reason for every scope
requirements.detail: Reviewers check why you request each scope, and scopes for features you have not built yet are not allowed.

steps.title: Create the Slack app
steps.detail: Sign in at api.slack.com/apps, create an app and choose your development workspace.

steps.title: Pick the smallest scope list
steps.detail: Bot scopes go in the scope parameter and user scopes in user_scope; request only what the feature uses today.

steps.title: Write the OAuth flow
steps.detail: Redirect to slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize, check the state value, then exchange the code at oauth.v2.access and store the token per workspace.

steps.title: Add scopes and the HTTPS redirect URL
steps.detail: Paste the scopes and redirect URL into OAuth & Permissions in the app settings.

steps.title: Install in your workspace and test
steps.detail: Run the Connect flow yourself and check the token can do what your agent needs.

steps.title: Turn on public distribution
steps.detail: Finish the checklist on the app's distribution page so other workspaces can install it as an unlisted app.

steps.title: Draft the Marketplace pack
steps.detail: Privacy policy, landing page, support page, scope reasons and the demo video script.

steps.title: Reach 10 workspaces, record the demo, submit
steps.detail: Pilot with unlisted installs until 10 workspaces are active, record the demo, then submit with test accounts and dummy data.

steps.title: Slack reviews the app
steps.detail: A preliminary review of up to 10 business days, then a functional review of up to 10 weeks. Slack cannot speed it up.

scopes.name: channels:read
scopes.meaning: List public channels and their members.

scopes.name: channels:history
scopes.meaning: Read messages in public channels. Unlisted apps get 1 request per minute on history calls.

scopes.name: im:history
scopes.meaning: Read direct messages. Marketplace reviewers expect a clear use case for broad history scopes.

scopes.name: search:read.public
scopes.meaning: User scope for searching public channel messages through Slack's MCP server.

scopes.name: search:read
scopes.meaning: Broad search over workspace data. Slack's Marketplace guide asks you not to request it.

limits.title: Unlisted apps: 1 history call per minute
limits.detail: Since 29 May 2025, new non-Marketplace apps get 1 request per minute and 15 objects per call on conversations.history and conversations.replies. Internal apps keep 50+ per minute.

limits.title: MCP needs an internal or Marketplace app
limits.detail: Only internal apps and Marketplace apps may use Slack's MCP server; unlisted apps are prohibited and there is no dynamic client registration.

limits.title: One message per second per channel
limits.detail: chat.postMessage generally allows one message per second per channel, plus a workspace-wide limit.

limits.title: Tokens do not expire by default
limits.detail: Slack OAuth tokens last until revoked unless you turn on token rotation, which gives you refresh tokens.

limits.title: Published apps are locked
limits.detail: After Marketplace approval, new scopes and redirect URLs only go live after another review, up to 6 weeks for changes.

blockers.fix: Use an HTTPS URL that matches the one saved in OAuth & Permissions exactly.

blockers.symptom: The Marketplace will not let you submit.
blockers.fix: You need 10+ active workspaces first: run a pilot with public (unlisted) distribution until you get there.

blockers.symptom: conversations.history returns ratelimited or only 15 messages.
blockers.fix: For your own workspace, build it as an internal app. For other workspaces, get Marketplace approval.

blockers.symptom: Slack's MCP server will not accept your app.
blockers.fix: Unlisted apps cannot use MCP: use an internal app in your workspace or publish to the Marketplace.

blockers.symptom: A workspace asks an admin to approve the Composio app.
blockers.fix: Ask the admin to approve it, or register your own Slack app and use those credentials in Composio.

sources.note: States no SSE and no dynamic client registration. Only internal or Marketplace apps.

sources.title: Slack MCP authorization server metadata
sources.note: HTTP 200. Issuer https://mcp.slack.com, authorize at slack.com/oauth/v2_user/authorize, token at oauth.v2.user.access, PKCE S256, client_secret_post. No registration_endpoint.

sources.title: Slack OpenID Connect discovery
sources.note: HTTP 200. Issuer https://slack.com, scopes openid, profile, email, grant authorization_code only. No registration_endpoint.

unverified: Slack never says outright that unlisted (public) distribution needs no review. Its docs only describe a review for Marketplace listings, so treat no review as implied.
The exact items in Slack's public distribution checklist are not listed in the docs we read.
When, or whether, the 1 request per minute history limit reached existing installs of older unlisted apps: the changelog says they are not impacted and gives no later date.
